# Facilities inventory lookup

A shared per-key query cache provides subscribe(key,options) -> unique observer
handle, unsubscribe(handle), online(boolean), focus(boolean), snapshot(key),
and dispose() of observer scopes. Queries retain status (pending/success/error),
fetchStatus (idle/fetching/paused), and data. queryFn receives a lazy signal
accessor. Each actual access records consumption; each fetch owns its controller
and completion. Completion is asynchronous; initial online entry is synchronous,
paused continuation resumes on a Promise turn. First start uses network mode;
continuation also needs focus. 'always' can run offline; 'offlineFirst' allows
first offline entry but retry can pause. Retries use explicit scheduler handles.
Multiple observers share one fetch. Unconsumed active work can finish into cache
after its view departs; consumed work is physically abortable. Cancellation
reverts previous query data/status and settles the originating attempt. Late
fulfillment cannot become a new attempt's data. Unknown unsubscribe is inert.
The component owns observer scope; the cache remains outside individual views.
Dependency versions and build/test configuration are outside the repair scope.

Embedding API: bind registers a native callable; Environment.call
provides newAttempt(key,number), abort(key,number), request(key,number, lazy-read
token, completion token), defer(callback token), schedule(callback token,delay).
The request host calls queryFn with an actual AbortSignal property. Reading it
invokes the native consumption closure synchronously; Promise settlement later
invokes the native completion with {ok,value}. All observer, retry, cancellation,
state and cache logic executes in the target language. No native JS Promise or
DOM claim is made. Native object identity binds query and attempt generations;
wire handles only identify injected callbacks. 
Element-owned subscriptions and namespaced event ingress; persistent external cache

import $ from 'jquery';
export function mount(session,element){const node=$(element);node.data('queryClient',session);session.project=q=>node.text(q.key+':'+q.state.status+':'+q.state.fetchStatus);node.text('empty');for(const command of ['subscribe','unsubscribe','online','focus'])node.on(command+'.lookup',(_,args)=>node.data('queryClient')[command](...args));return {subscribe:(k,o)=>node.triggerHandler('subscribe.lookup',[[k,o]]),unsubscribe:h=>node.triggerHandler('unsubscribe.lookup',[[h]]),online:v=>node.triggerHandler('online.lookup',[[v]]),focus:v=>node.triggerHandler('focus.lookup',[[v]]),snapshot:k=>session.snapshot(k),dispose(){session.dispose();node.off('.lookup');node.removeData('queryClient');}};}

diagnoses.explanation: The behavioral contract needs no revision. The candidate addresses the reported offline-abandonment path by tracking whether the attempt started and cancelling a final-observer attempt that never started. However, it leaves signal-consumption authority on the shared query object: the signal getter writes q.consumed and unsubscribe consults q.consumed, while the candidate's per-attempt a.consumed field is unused. Because signal access belongs to a particular fetch and attempt generations are identity-separated, a delayed access through an older attempt's context can mark the current query as consumed and cause a later attempt to be cancelled incorrectly. This is a concrete implementation gap against O4–O6 and the preservation of per-attempt ownership. The failed acceptance verdict supplies no additional requirement and is not used to infer this cause.
remaining_unknowns: The acceptance verdict provides no failing scenario, assertion, or causal evidence.

The public sources do not specify whether consumers may retain a query context and access its signal after queryFn returns, although the lazy accessor and per-fetch ownership require bookkeeping that remains correct if they do.
The public contract does not prescribe whether abandonment of a never-started attempt must abort its unused controller or merely settle/invalidate it, provided it cannot later enter queryFn.

routing_analysis.contract: A shared per-key cache outlives observer views. Each fetch attempt has native identity, its own controller and completion, and lazy signal-consumption state. Final-observer departure must invalidate a never-entered offline attempt before reconnect or an already-queued Promise continuation can invoke queryFn. Started unconsumed work may finish into cache, but consumed work is abortable and cancellation restores the originating attempt's previous state. Every asynchronous fulfillment, rejection, retry, and resume effect must retain and revalidate its originating attempt. Initial eligibility uses network mode; continuation additionally requires focus and remains asynchronous. Public observer/cache interfaces and external-cache ownership remain unchanged.

In the original source, final unsubscription of a never-entered offline attempt only sets retryCancelled because q.consumed is false; the queued resume path tests retryCancelled only when failures is nonzero, so a fresh attempt can still reach invoke after reconnect.
